Standing-grant matching ignores the tool digest: USE_APPROVAL_SCOPE_GRANT_SQL matches tool name, action key and class only. Bind grants to the digest, or revoke on drift, before enabling standing grants for MCP tools.
The rule-use audit row tool_policy_rule_used is not built. It needs a durable sink reachable from execution-core, and capability-core EvaluatePolicy carries no ZDR posture.
tool_policy_rule_expired is not built: an expired allow is demoted to ask silently. A sweeper or read-path writer is needed, and it must be content-free.

The 90-day default and 365-day cap apply to every allow written through PUT, not only Always rules, and this is not behind a switch. Legacy allow rows have no expiry and never lapse; the owner should decide on a backfill.

Always cannot be reached end to end: no approval producer sets ApprovalCause.tool_digest (agent.rs and grpc.rs still call approval_cause::for_call), so is_pinned_mcp is false for every live cause and rule_offered never holds.

eligible_scopes now offers thread/run for a pinned MCP external_write, but the standing-grant match (USE_APPROVAL_SCOPE_GRANT_SQL) keys on tool, action_key and class only, not tool_digest. A thread grant would therefore survive a definition drift for its TTL. Bind grants to the digest before APPROVAL_SCOPE_GRANTS_ENABLED and the digest producers are switched on.

Some capability-core changes are not behind any switch. Every allow written through PUT /v1/tool-policies now gets a 90-day default lapse (365-day cap), and its audit action is renamed from tool_policy_set to tool_policy_rule_created/confirmed. With TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED on and APPROVAL_RULE_PROPOSALS_ENABLED off, behaviour therefore differs from HEAD for manually set allows. The owner must accept this, or the lapse must be scoped to Always rules.

ZDR/DEC-32: a confirmed user allow in capability-core applies to any later run, including ZDR or waived runs, and EvaluatePolicy carries no ZDR posture. Decide whether those runs may use a rule, and make any rule-use audit row ZDR-aware before the switch is flipped.

The flag row says APPROVAL_RULE_PROPOSALS_ENABLED requires WS05 TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED, but model-gateway checked_rule_proposal does not check that. With the proposals switch on and enforcement off, a person can confirm a rule that never applies.

ApprovalRuleProposals.tsx, confirmApprovalRule and ruleConfirmationRequest are not mounted or called anywhere outside their tests, so they are dead code until the settings mount and the proposal list land. The confirm write also has no action contract in src/shared/actions (project rule).
Legacy allow rows keep expires_at NULL and never lapse. Only new writes get the 90-day lapse, so the owner should decide on a backfill.

The plan's named tests confirming_writes_a_digest_pinned_allow and a_digest_drift_demotes_the_rule_to_ask exist only as equivalents: the FE test 'confirming writes a digest-pinned allow that lapses in ninety days' and Go TestADigestDriftDemotesTheRuleToAsk. No server-side test checks that a confirm is refused when the proposal digest differs from the registry pin.
setToolPolicySQL labels any allow written over an existing active row (for example an ask) as tool_policy_rule_confirmed, although no rule existed before. The audit label then misstates the history.
